title: The Best Detention
premise: Beatrix Galloway has spent seventeen years perfecting the art of being unnoticed, channeling everything they can't say into loaves of bread that taste like grief, hope, and longing. When their senior English teacher assigns a college essay on 'the one thing you'd fight to keep,' Beatrix writes about Hollowbrook's Founders' Bake—a century-old tradition where every family bakes a truth into a communal loaf—and accidentally submits it. The essay wins a contest, goes viral locally, and exposes that the bake's founding charter is about to be sold off by a developer who happens to be Beatrix's estranged father's business partner. As Beatrix organizes students, bakers, and skeptics to save the tradition, they discover the bake itself holds a secret: their grandmother's original recipe, hidden in the town archive, proves the Galloways were among the founders their father has spent his life erasing. In the climax, during the final bake before the land auction, Beatrix publicly reads their essay from atop the flour mill, forcing the town—and their father—to choose between profit and belonging; the charter is saved by a community-funded buyout, and Beatrix finally signs their name to something instead of hiding it.
about_author: Astrid Nystrom grew up above her family's bakery in coastal Maine, where she learned that dough rises best when you stop punching it down. She writes stories about quiet kids who discover that silence was always a kind of loud.

chapters.title: The Invisible Loaf
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. We meet them at 5 a.m. in Galloway Bakery, kneading a loaf laced with homesickness for a customer who just lost her dog—baking feelings is the family gift nobody talks about. At school, Beatrix executes their invisibility routine flawlessly. Emotional beat: comfort in concealment, with hairline cracks showing.

chapters.title: One Honest Question
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. English teacher Ms. Okafor assigns the college essay: 'What would you fight to keep?' Beatrix freezes at the prompt, then writes three pages about the Founders' Bake at 2 a.m., planning to delete it. They don't. Emotional beat: the terrifying relief of writing one true sentence.

chapters.title: Submitted by Accident
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. A mouse-click mishap sends the essay to a regional youth writing contest. Panic spirals through the bakery as Beatrix tries to recall it and fails. Their mother, Marisol, notices something changed in her kid's shoulders. Emotional beat: dread braided with a flicker of wanting to be seen.

chapters.title: Locker Shut, Door Open
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. The essay wins. The local paper runs an excerpt naming Beatrix and the Founders' Bake. Classmates who've never spoken to them now do—including Priya Chandrasekaran, editor of the school paper, who smells a bigger story. Emotional beat: exposure like sunburn, painful but warm.

chapters.title: The For-Sale Sign
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Investigating the bake's history for her article, Priya discovers the mill green where the Founders' Bake happens is listed for sale by Halloway Development. She brings the deed to Beatrix, who recognizes the developer's partner's name: their father, Edmund Galloway, gone eleven years. Emotional beat: the personal colliding with the civic.

chapters.title: Bread Remembers
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Beatrix confronts their mother, who finally explains: the Galloways were founding families of the bake, until Edmund left and legally severed the name from the charter. Marisol kept baking truths into bread anyway. Emotional beat: inherited shame cracking open into inherited pride.

chapters.title: Recruiting the Skeptics
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya and Beatrix form a ragtag committee: jaded student council president Theo, elderly baker Mr. Fenwick, and Beatrix's little brother Milo, who can't keep a secret. First meeting in the bakery back room draws exactly six people. Emotional beat: fragile coalition, comic friction, first sparks of purpose.

chapters.title: What My Father Baked
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Beatrix finds Edmund's name in the 1974 bake ledger—the year he entered a loaf no one ate, labeled only 'LEAVING.' The discovery humanizes him against Beatrix's will. Flashbacks via Marisol's storytelling. Emotional beat: rage complicated by grief.

chapters.title: Petition and Pushback
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. The committee gathers 400 signatures, but the town council defers to the sale contract, and Halloway Development counters with promises of jobs. Theo, whose family needs those jobs, wavers publicly. Emotional beat: the cost of principle when survival is on the table.

chapters.title: The Essay Goes Around
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya publishes the full essay in the school paper; it spreads through town group chats. Strangers start leaving notes in Beatrix's locker sharing what they'd fight to keep. Beatrix, overwhelmed, hides in the walk-in freezer. Emotional beat: visibility as both gift and ambush.

chapters.title: Edmund Comes to Town
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Edmund arrives for a development photo-op and requests coffee with Beatrix. Over untouched pastries, he offers to 'protect' the bake by relocating it to a mall atrium—in exchange for Beatrix publicly endorsing the project. Emotional beat: seduction of the easy way out.

chapters.title: A Loaf of No
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Beatrix bakes their answer to Edmund—a dense, bitter rye—and delivers it to his hotel without a note. He knows. That night Marisol reveals the charter requires all founding-family descendants' consent to alter the bake's terms, and Edmund's signature is the last missing piece. Emotional beat: defiance as inheritance.

chapters.title: Archive Dust
chapters.summary: Milo's POV. Milo, banned from meetings but not from curiosity, sneaks into the town archive hunting proof and finds a sealed tin: Grandmother Ada Galloway's original bake recipe and a letter insisting 'the loaf must be baked where the wheat was grown.' The mill green is that ground. Emotional beat: the smallest ally lands the biggest blow.

chapters.title: Legal Yeast
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. With the letter, the committee finds a pro bono lawyer: the recipe predates the land's rezoning, potentially voiding the sale. But proving it requires the bake to physically occur on the green before the auction date—which falls on this year's bake day, moved up deliberately. Emotional beat: hope with a ticking clock.

chapters.title: Divided Dough
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo's father takes a Halloway job; Theo resigns from the committee, then un-resigns after his father quietly tells him to fight for something worth having. The committee fractures over tactics: petition versus spectacle. Emotional beat: loyalty tested, repaired imperfectly.

chapters.title: The Night Before
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Bake-eve. The whole town seems to hold its breath; volunteers prep in the dark mill while Halloway crews fence half the green. Beatrix calls Edmund and asks him, plainly, to come watch them bake. No argument, just the invitation. Emotional beat: stillness before the storm, courage chosen rather than felt.

chapters.title: The Last Founders' Bake
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs interwoven. Dawn breaks; hundreds arrive, each carrying dough holding a truth. The bake proceeds under threat of trespass citations as the sheriff hesitates before a crowd of grandmothers. Beatrix kneads the master loaf with shaking hands. Emotional beat: collective heartbeat, terror transmuted into ritual.

chapters.title: Read It From the Mill
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. As the auctioneer's tent pitches at the green's edge, Beatrix climbs the flour mill and reads their essay aloud through a megaphone—the whole town silent except the river. Then they read Ada Galloway's letter. Edmund steps out of the crowd. Emotional beat: the climax of voice, the moment invisibility dies.

chapters.title: His Signature
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Edmund, confronted by the ledger page bearing his own teenage handwriting, refuses—then sees the loaf labeled LEAVING recreated by Beatrix and placed in his hands. He tears up the partnership agreement instead of signing consent, walking away from Halloway. Emotional beat: forgiveness neither cheap nor complete.

chapters.title: Community Rising
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. With the sale voided pending litigation, Theo proposes the community land trust; the town funds it in forty-eight hours—bakeries, churches, even rival developers hedging their image. The charter is amended to include every family, old and new. Emotional beat: victory as shared labor, not miracle.

chapters.title: The Best Detention
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Beatrix gets Saturday detention for the megaphone stunt—served, at Ms. Okafor's arrangement, in the bakery teaching detention-mates to knead. Beatrix submits the final college essay unchanged, signed proudly. Emotional beat: punishment reframed as belonging; identity claimed.

chapters.title: Where the Wheat Was Grown
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV, epilogue tone. Spring: the Founders' Bake continues on the saved green, now with Beatrix's name carved beside Ada's on the charter stone. Edmund helps Milo plant wheat at the field's edge, unasked and unwelcome and present. Beatrix bakes a loaf with no feeling hidden in it—just bread, shared openly. Emotional beat: full-circle peace, roots and wings at once.
